headline: Trump says he'll lift the tariff on Irish whiskey
summary: He announced it at his golf resort in Doonbeg, Ireland, before handing the Irish Open trophy to Shane Lowry. Whiskey made in the Republic of Ireland pays the tariff the US charges on European Union goods. Whiskey from Northern Ireland has paid none since May. Trump said the Irish prime minister and Lowry both asked him to drop it.

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: When something comes into our country from another one, the government can charge extra money for it. That's called a tariff. It's like a toll for crossing a bridge. Today the president said a grown-up drink from Ireland won't pay that toll anymore, and nothing changes for you.
5-7.why: Five-year-olds don't know what whiskey is, and they don't need to. The toll is the whole idea, and it's a small one.
5-7.why_long: A five-year-old has no idea what whiskey is and does not need one. A toll they can hold: you cross, you pay, someone said stop paying. The script keeps the story inside that one picture and ends where their interest does, which is whether anything changes for them. Nothing does.

8-12.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
8-12.script: A tariff is a fee a country charges on goods coming in from abroad. In May, Trump dropped it for UK whiskey, which covers Northern Ireland. Whiskey from the Republic of Ireland kept paying, so distillers just north had an edge. Today he said he'll drop it for Ireland too. Like a referee resetting the line after a head start.
8-12.why: Kids this age track fairness closely. Two neighbors, one fee, then none, is a chain they can follow and argue about.
8-12.why_long: Two distillers a few miles apart, one paying the fee and one not, is what a ten-year-old fixes on. This is the age for it: they are working out whether a rule lands on everybody the same. The script gives the sequence and stops. Expect “why did the other one get out first?” Because Northern Ireland is in the UK.

13-17.script: Is "everybody's been bugging me" a good reason to drop a tax? That's how Trump explained lifting the tariff on Irish whiskey, speaking at his own golf resort after the Irish prime minister and a golfer asked him. Who gains from a decision made that way, and who should have been in the room?
13-17.why: Teenagers spot the mix of personal and public here on their own. Let them say what bothers them, or doesn't, before you do.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold the decision and the reason given for it apart, and that gap is the story here. A tax dropped at the man’s own golf resort after a prime minister and a golfer asked him. The script lays out who asked and where. Ask what bothers them about it before you say what bothers you.

5-7.a: A strong drink for grown-ups. Kids don't have it. This story is really about the money, not the drink.

8-12.a: The company bringing the goods into the country. It often adds that cost to the price, so shoppers end up paying part of it.

8-12.q: Why did Northern Ireland get a break first?
8-12.a: It's part of the UK, and Trump dropped tariffs on UK whiskey in May. The Republic of Ireland is in the EU, so it kept paying.

13-17.q: Can a president cancel a tariff just by announcing it?
13-17.a: He said he will. The report doesn't say when or how. Worth watching whether it actually happens.

13-17.q: Isn't it odd he announced it at his own golf course?
13-17.a: He did, and thousands protested his visit too. A local businessman says the course employs 300 people. Hold both facts and see what you think.
